Answer: B
Reason: The question describes specific radiographic signs of pneumopericardium (varying cardiac density, abnormal bulge, translucent line outlining mediastinum) resulting from a penetrating stab wound; among the choices, rupture of the ascending aorta or pulmonary trunk is the only option representing a catastrophic perforation of a great vessel that would introduce air into the pericardial sac and cause these findings.
